opex.name: Sales and marketing
opex.note: Selling the platform and winning new merchants. Up 18% YoY.

opex.name: Research and development
opex.note: Building the platform and new commerce and AI features. Up 13% YoY.

opex.name: General and administrative
opex.note: The back office — finance, legal and admin. Up 103% YoY, but only because Q2 2024 included a $55M legal-liability reversal.

opex.name: Transaction and loan losses
opex.note: Losses on merchant loans and cash advances, and transaction losses. Up 90% YoY as more sales flowed through Shopify Payments.

follow100Note: Merchant solutions brings in $75.52 of every $100 — mostly a cut of merchants' sales — but direct costs eat $51.42 of every $100 overall. Paper gains on equity investments added $30.30 of every $100 this quarter, which is why profit kept ($33.81) is far above operating profit alone. Rows may not add exactly due to rounding.
footerNote: The earnings release prints a condensed statement (operating income $291M, net other income including taxes of $615M, net income $906M); the split of that $615M into other income, the equity-method loss and tax comes from the detailed statement in Shopify's Form 10-Q filed the same day, as the release itself directs.
oneTimers: A $568M after-tax paper gain from equity investments: a $681M unrealized (paper) gain on equity and other investments and a $1M realized gain, partly offset by a $24M loss on its equity-method investment. Shopify says net income excluding the impact of equity investments was $338M (non-GAAP), versus $906M GAAP.

G&A looks like it doubled (+103% to $122M) only because a year ago Shopify released a $55M accrual for an estimated legal liability; on that basis underlying G&A rose about 6%. Shopify also booked a $10M impairment charge on right-of-use assets and leasehold improvements this quarter.
otherDetail: Other income of $788M in total: $681M of unrealized (paper) gains on equity and other investments, $106M of interest income, a $24M foreign-exchange gain and a $1M realized gain. The $24M equity-method loss is the separate equityM line; the rest nets to otherIncomeM of $812M.
pngFooterNote: Paper gains on equity stakes swelled the bottom line.

segments.name: Subscription solutions
segments.note: The monthly plans merchants pay to run their stores on Shopify. Up 17% YoY; monthly recurring revenue reached $185M.

segments.name: Merchant solutions
segments.note: Mostly payment processing (Shopify Payments) — a cut of the sales flowing through merchants' stores — plus shipping and other merchant services. Up 37% YoY and 76% of all revenue.

sources.label: Form 10-Q — detailed statements of operations (SEC EDGAR)

takeaways.text: Revenue rose 31% to $2.68B, up from 21% growth a year ago, as GMV grew 31% to $87.8B. Growth accelerated in North America, Europe and Asia Pacific; Europe GMV grew 42% on a constant-currency basis. Merchant solutions led, up 37% to $2.02B, while subscription revenue grew 17% to $656M and monthly recurring revenue reached $185M.
takeaways.title: Growth accelerated again

takeaways.text: Free cash flow was $422M — 16% of revenue, the eighth straight quarter of double-digit free cash flow margins — from $428M of operating cash flow and just $6M of capital spending (capex — money spent on property and equipment). Operating income rose 21% to $291M.
takeaways.title: Cash generation stayed strong

takeaways.text: Net income jumped to $906M from $171M a year ago, but $568M of that (after tax) was a paper gain on equity investments — a $681M unrealized gain, versus a $79M paper loss a year ago — plus a $24M equity-method loss. Excluding equity investments, net income was $338M, up from $291M a year ago.
takeaways.title: Paper gains inflated the bottom line

verdict: Shopify grew revenue 31% to $2.7B and generated $422M of free cash flow, while a $681M paper gain on equity investments lifted net income to $906M — far above the $338M earned excluding those investments.
